investigation.title: Remote Agent Swarm Gateway 502 — All Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared Upstream Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-13T01:09:08–42Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because every check shares the same error message and no evidence was collected, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway layer, not to individual check logic or the eval runner itself.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing POST /api/agents (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents) returned a 502 bad_gateway during the eval run window, preventing agent provisioning from starting. This caused all three remote-agent checks to fail before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) could be collected. The failure is an infrastructure-layer connectivity issue between the production API and the swarm ELB endpoint, not a defect in the eval runner or expected-output contract definitions. No historical pass data exists to establish a regression baseline, and no suspect code changes are identified in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges.
